what_is_actually_running.model: Whisper large-v2 (OpenAI speech-to-text), HuggingFace ASR build
what_is_actually_running.weights_origin: s3://jumpstart-cache-prod-us-east-1/... -- AWS's own PUBLIC JumpStart cache, not a customer bucket. No fine-tuning, no private data, no artifact of ours is inside this endpoint.
what_is_actually_running.provenance: A one-click JumpStart deploy from SageMaker Studio. The 'jumpstart-dft-' prefix is the default name JumpStart generates (dft = default).

belongs_to.conclusion: Every identity involved predates this project by 4+ years. This is a resource we FOUND, not one we caused.

what_is_actually_running.ownership_tags: NONE. The only tags are JumpStart's automatic model-id/domain/user-profile tags -- no owner, no cost centre, no project. That absence is exactly why a sweep restricted to `llmops-*` could never have found it: there is nothing on it to claim.

utilization_90d.reading: The A10G never ran a single inference. The 6.6% memory is the model weights sitting resident. It idled for 843 days -- 2024-04-11 creation to 2026-08-02 deletion. The window measured here is only the last 90 of those; CloudWatch does not retain further back, so '0 invocations' is proven for 90 days and inferred for the rest from 0 CloudTrail InvokeEndpoint events.

pause_is_impossible_verified.list_inference_components: 0 -- this is a legacy ProductionVariant endpoint, not the Inference-Component architecture that supports scale-to-zero
pause_is_impossible_verified.ManagedInstanceScaling: not configured on the variant or the config
pause_is_impossible_verified.conclusion: Checked rather than assumed. Neither scale-to-zero nor a desired-count of 0 is available here, so stopping the bill means deleting the endpoint. Substituting delete for a user's 'pause' is a scope change that needs their explicit word, not the agent's inference.

cost_measured.source: Cost Explorer USAGE_TYPE USE1-Host:ml.g5.2xlarge -- $36.36 on each of seven consecutive full days, and $1.515 on the partial day 2026-08-01. NOT a JumpStart-default estimate; the first sweep's $18/day guess was half this.
cost_measured.not_covered_by_the_account_budget: bedrock-monthly-dev is filtered to Service: ["Amazon Bedrock"], so no account-level control would ever have flagged this. See docs/COST.md section 10.

note: SageMaker real-time endpoints cannot be paused (verified above, not assumed): the minimum is one instance, so stopping the bill means deleting the endpoint. The EndpointConfig and Model below are NOT deleted -- and both are free to keep. Recreating the endpoint from them is a single create_endpoint call (~5-8 min to InService), and the weights live in AWS's public cache, so nothing needs re-uploading.
restore: aws sagemaker create-endpoint --endpoint-name jumpstart-dft-hf-asr-whisper-large-v2 --endpoint-config-name jumpstart-dft-hf-asr-whisper-large-v2 --region us-east-1
status: DELETED 2026-08-02 on the owner's explicit authorization. delete_endpoint returned, status went Deleting, and list_endpoints in us-east-1 now returns ZERO endpoints. The owner's original instruction said 'pause'; pause does not exist here (see pause_is_impossible_verified), so deletion waited for them to say it in as many words rather than being inferred from technical necessity.

restore_path_verified_after_delete.weights: s3://jumpstart-cache-prod-us-east-1/... still AWS's public cache; nothing of ours needed re-uploading
restore_path_verified_after_delete.note: Checked AFTER the delete, not before. 'Reversible' was a claim until these two describes returned; both objects are free to keep, so the one-line restore above is a fact rather than an intention.
